subject: Post-demo: Cloud delta & 1M-token cost breakdown + next tests
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha@quantasecurity.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + cost comparison asks

Thanks for the demo earlier — nice walk-through. A few things we need to validate before we show this to procurement and our platform team:  

1) Straight per-1M token cost comparison vs our hyperscaler credits (they quoted us as low as $0.60 per 1M tokens for a compressed model path). Please call out assumptions (batch size, sequence length, kv/prefix cache behavior).
2) Latency SLO impact when moving from batch=1 to batch=8 (99th pct target 250ms).
3) How cache hit rates translate to effective token unit economics (we get bursty traffic with ~35% repeat prefix hits for chat).
4) Any differences for private deployment vs hosted API for pricing and routing.

Can you share a concise breakdown + proposed next-tests (what we need to provide and expected outputs)? Also our security team will send a short SOC2 questionnaire next.

Thanks,
Sasha
Head of Platform
Quantasec

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha@quantasecurity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + cost comparison asks

Great to meet, Sasha — appreciate the clear asks. Summary + plan below. I attached a compact spreadsheet (redwood-pricing-vs-hyperscaler.xlsx) and a proposed test plan (quantasec-eval-test-plan.yaml).

Recap (assumptions called out)
- Reference workload: chat session average seq len 180 tokens; 60% of sessions have short follow-ups (prefix reuse).
- Hyperscaler quote you referenced: $0.60 / 1M tokens (unclear if batching or prefix cache assumed; their published numbers often assume unbatched, static batching).
- Redwood preliminary model path (quantized): $0.28 / 1M tokens @ 50% observed cache hit (prefix + KV reuse); heavy batching scenarios drop unit cost further but may increase tail latency.

Key differentiators we expect to impact your numbers
- Prefix/KV caching: our default prefix cache + client-side sticky routing gives higher effective cache hit for conversational sessions (we see +20-40% hit vs naïve setups).
- Smart routing + fallback: will route by latency vs cost; you can pin critical traffic to Dedicated pools to meet 99th pct.
- Quantization profiles: our inference runtime supports mixed precision / int8 paths that reduce GPU token cost without large quality loss for your models.

Proposed next-tests (what we need from Quantasec)
- Provide a ~24h sample of anonymized request traces (timestamps, sequence length, repeat-prefix hash) — helps estimate realistic cache-hit distribution.
- Target KPI matrix: 99th pct latency <= 250ms, mean latency <= 85ms, and cost target <$0.40 / 1M tokens for interactive traffic.
- Test vectors: 10k sessions, mix A (90% read/followup), mix B (burst peak 10x baseline).

What we will run / deliver
- A 72h probe in our hosted staging with: batch sweep {1,2,4,8}, cache on/off, quantization off/on.
- Deliverables: per-sweep cost-per-1M tokens, P50/P95/P99 latency, measured cache hit rate, recommended config for production (batch, cache TTL, routing policy).
- Optional: Dedicated pool cost estimate if you need committed throughput and stricter SLOs.

Next steps / asks
1) Sasha — share the anonymized trace sample (we can accept a zipped CSV).
2) Sasha — legal will want an NDA / SOW for dedicated testing. We included a DocuSign link in related_links for streamlined signature; let me know if you prefer your procurement flow.
3) Marissa / Ben — can you confirm SOC2 artifact availability and whether our shared drive link can host relevant evidence for Quantasec?

Thanks — I left short notes in the spreadsheet where the $/1M calc lives. Happy to run a 30m call to walk the test plan through.

—
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 04 Oct 2028 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up + cost comparison asks

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Quantasec asks and our plan. Quick internal checklist before we run the staged probe: 

- Marissa: can you confirm which SOC2 artifacts (Type II infra controls + encryption in transit keys) we can share via our secure portal? Quantasec legal may request a copy.
- Ben: SE please size the Dedicated pool estimate if they want commit for 100 RPS sustained (~peak 1k RPS bursts). Include monthly commit and burst pricing in the spreadsheet.
- SE test request: run batch-sweep scripts and return this matrix: {batch, cache=true/false, tokens_processed, average_gpu_util, p99_latency, measured_cache_hit}.

Also: flag any model quantization caveats. I annotated the spreadsheet lines where int8 path might need small quality checks for their hallucination-sensitive prompts.

R — fyi I recommended the 72h hosted probe first (fastest data) and then propose a 7d Dedicated smoke if they like the numbers.

—
Rafael

From: Sasha Patel <sasha@quantasecurity.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>
Cc: Quantasec Legal <legal@quantasecurity.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + cost comparison asks

Thanks Rafael — that plan looks actionable. We will: 
- Share anonymized 24h traces by EOD Monday (zipped CSV).
- Legal will review the SOC2 portal link; if needed we can sign the NDA via your DocuSign link.
- We'll take the 72h hosted probe first to validate cost delta and cache behavior. If numbers check out we'll scope Dedicated commit.

Two quick clarifications: 
1) Can you include the baseline hyperscaler assumptions in the spreadsheet (their stated batch model / tokenization assumptions)? That will help our procurement team reconcile quotes.
2) For the 72h probe, please include a breakdown that normalizes to per-1M tokens after applying measured cache hit (so procurement sees the "effective" per-1M number).

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to run a short sync next week after you get the traces.

Best,
Sasha
Head of Platform
Quantasec
